source_review.notes: Reviewed GraphBLAS 2.1.0, primary Ligra and current GBBS, NVIDIA sparse-format documentation, Unicode normalization, the Stanford IR text, maintained Lucene codecs and PISA, Princeton suffix-array material, and the primary ART paper. All ten final destinations returned HTTP 200.

evidence: Checked hard requirement/capability sets, graph n/m, text document/token/vocabulary quantities, final/peak/delta/retained bytes, generations, and amplification ratios.
Checked canonical facts, derived views, external IDs, dense generation indices, physical slots, analyzer coordinates, snapshots, and ADR evidence remain distinct.
notation_and_syntax.notes: All ratios and byte formulas name their modeled fields and exclusions.

evidence: Recomputed CSR+CSC structural bytes 96,000,016 and one-bit matrix ceil(10^12/8)=125,000,000,000.
Recomputed integer matrix-to-CSR+CSC ratio 1302.
Recomputed graph feasible candidates and minimum modeled feasible choice CSR+CSC for in/out/scan.
Recomputed only inverted+trie covers term/phrase/prefix in the finite text candidate set.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Modeled bytes deliberately exclude properties, mappings, alignment, temporary buffers, caches, and retained generations and are labeled accordingly.

evidence: Verified semantic and hard-capability feasibility precede cost/performance comparison.
Verified canonical-to-derived correctness requires logical equality and stable-ID/coordinate mappings under one generation.
Verified immutable base plus delta shifts work between read merge and rebuild/space/write amplification without changing required snapshots.
Verified output-sensitive operations and peak old+new+temporary+retained bytes invalidate navigation-only/final-only cost claims.
Verified dominance and ADR conclusions remain conditional on evidence uncertainty, workload, and hard constraints.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The chapter presents a decision process rather than a theorem selecting one universal representation.

evidence: Reviewed empty/dense/sparse/skewed/hub/partitioned graphs; direction, loops, parallels, zero properties, ID remaps, high-degree output, and accelerator/NUMA placement.
Reviewed raw/analyzed/prefix/substring text identity, Unicode/analyzer changes, common/rare terms, long prefixes, phrase positions, cross-document/tenant spans, and large outputs.

Reviewed n^2/byte/count/offset overflow, final-versus-peak capacity, delta/merge debt, mixed generations, stalled readers, cold pages, partial publication, crash/rollback, hostile parsers, authorization timing, and query amplification.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Revisit triggers explicitly cover growth, workload shifts, tail latency, capacity, schema/analyzer, incidents, and dependency lifecycle.

evidence: The executable constructs explicit capability sets and admits candidates only when required sets are subsets.
It independently recomputes structural bytes, selects the smallest modeled feasible graph candidate, and verifies final coverage for graph/text choices.
The chapter requires cross-view reconstruction, logical references, generation manifests, and evidence paths rather than relying on the decision trace alone.
invariant_checking.notes: The finite trace is capability/byte arithmetic, not a benchmark, workload emulator, or production architecture validator.

evidence: Reviewed semantic/operation/workload contracts, concrete and peak byte models, capability feasibility, canonical/derived ownership, updates/deltas/partitions, and durability boundaries.
Reviewed analytical versus measured operations, tail/counter/environment evidence, correctness/fault/concurrency/security reviews, ADR content, triggers, and migration.
Reviewed graph and text decision patterns, analyzer/substring distinctions, authorization, parser/resource safety, immutable recovery, observability, and external-review boundaries.
proof_review.notes: A candidate is never accepted from asymptotics or one average benchmark alone.

evidence: Structural byte arithmetic, capability feasibility, logical cross-view proofs, benchmark evidence, and operational judgments are labeled separately.
Graph/text library and paper behavior is attached to named official/primary references.
The executable and examples explicitly state modeled exclusions and scoped workloads.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: No universal CSR, matrix, inverted, trie, suffix, codec, or hybrid superiority claim is made.

evidence: The standard-library-only Python trace passed exact fifteen-line stdout, empty stderr, and zero exit status under the recorded Python toolchain.
It emits evidence=finite_representation_decision_trace and checks formulas, hard capability rejection, feasible choice, and requirement coverage.
All ten final external destinations returned HTTP 200 and repository-local links passed module validation.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No representative graph/text benchmark, actual full/peak bytes, concurrency, durability, authorization, recovery, relevance, security, or production tail behavior was empirically evaluated.

conceptual_review.notes: Synthesizes Level-I graph/text structures into a gated workflow: semantic inventory, operation/workload contract, byte/peak model, capabilities, canonical/derived views, lifecycle, measurements, evidence, ADR, triggers, and migration.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed stable external IDs, exact field/edge semantics, concrete capacity including rebuild overlap, segment/partition/delta operations, atomic manifests, visibility/durability, tail and counter evidence, shadow validation, rollback, security budgets, observability, ownership, and measurable revisit criteria.

pedagogical_review.notes: Integrates DSE-041 through DSE-049 without collapsing their distinct semantics, leads with rejection of infeasible choices, includes a reproducible scoped model, ten examples, and five architecture exercises with complete answers.

limitations: Internal authoring, primary/official-source, mathematical, executable-snippet, conceptual, practitioner, and pedagogical evidence only; no external academic, GraphBLAS, Ligra, GBBS, NVIDIA, Unicode, Stanford IR, Lucene, PISA, Princeton, ART, security, performance, relevance, reliability, operations, architecture, cost, or independent practitioner review is claimed. The chapter and finite trace prove neither full production byte/capacity models, representative workload performance, universal representation choice, arbitrary graph/text semantics, cross-view implementation correctness, fixed-width/allocation/failure safety, concurrent snapshot/reclamation, durable publication/crash recovery, authorization noninterference, hostile-parser security, production cache/NUMA/storage/tail behavior, certification, nor deployment fitness.
